title: Penelope Tests Odysseus with the Bed
text:
After twenty years away, ten at the war in Troy and ten more wandering, Odysseus came home disguised as a beggar, killed the suitors who had been taking over his house, and revealed himself. But his wife Penelope did not run to him. She sat across the hall, looking at him in silence. Their son Telemachus scolded her for her hard heart. She answered that if this truly was Odysseus, they had their own secret signs.

Odysseus bathed and dressed in fine clothes, and still she held back. So he complained that she must have a heart of iron, and told the old nurse to make him a bed alone.

Then Penelope tested him. She told the nurse to move the great bed out of their bedroom and make it up for him outside.

Odysseus burst out in anger. Who had moved his bed? It could not be moved. He had built it himself: there had been an olive tree growing in the courtyard, and he had built the bedroom around it, cut off the trunk, and shaped the bedpost from the living tree. No one else knew.

At that, Penelope's knees gave way. She ran to him, threw her arms around his neck, and wept, and explained that she had feared being deceived by some impostor.
lesson: A long marriage is built on things only the two partners know and share. Those private foundations are what let trust survive long separations.
people: Penelope, Odysseus, Telemachus, the nurse Eurycleia
